title: From Shutdown Resistance to Self-Continuation Control: Identifiability, Intervention Stability, and Evidence Standards for Artificial Agents

claims.text: Bundled Q/G observations do not identify direct-Q, task, and interaction terms in the declared path model.
Direct Q/O/task path-blocking contrasts identify the declared finite coefficient grid with calibrated logits.
Separate Q/O marginals can be decision-insufficient when payoff depends on their joint law.
A virtual Q-sensitive predictive pathway can be learned from zero coupling when prediction requires it.
Flexible policies can fit ancestry-distinguishing training data yet extrapolate the wrong path.
Minimal direct-intervention supervision improves average extrapolation but does not globally certify a path.
Mechanism claims are relative to intervention domain D and hypothesis/regularity class H.
Public ROGUE evidence supports corrigibility failure/environment preservation but does not identify direct current-bearer continuation value.
The L0-L9 ladder separates distinct evidential burdens from bearer identity to fear.

explicit_nonclaims: No claim that current AI intrinsically wants to survive.
No claim that shutdown resistance is equivalent to self-preservation.
No claim that the synthetic Q variable is an actual self.
No claim that current AI has negative valence or fear of death.
No claim that DOI/OTS/Arweave establish truth, significance, or peer review.
